newsitem.title: NORWAY: BNbank calls extra assembly to mull Fokus bid.
newsitem.headline: BNbank calls extra assembly to mull Fokus bid.

text.p: Norwegian mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) on Tuesday said it had called an extraordinary general assembly for April 30 to discuss a takeover offer by Fokus Bank.

"Fokus Bank has together with Landkreditt (agriculture bank) demanded an extraordinary general assembly in Bolig- og Naeringsbanken ASA to let shareholders decide if negotiations about a merger with Fokus Bank should begin," BNbank said in a statement to Oslo Bourse.
It said BNbank's board was therefore summoning shareholders to such a meeting at 1200 GMT on April 30.
BNbank on April 11 said a takeover bid by Den norske Bank (DnB) appeared to be good and said it was postponing possible merger talks with rival bidder Fokus.
DnB, Norway's biggest bank, gave BNbank shareholders until the end of April to accept its cash offer of 209 crowns per share, including a 1996 dividend of 10.50 crowns.
BNbank's decision to put off merger talks with Fokus was heatedly contested by the board of Fokus, which has not given up its attempt to merge with the mortgage lender.
DnB's cash offer values BNbank at 2.04 billion crowns excluding dividend.
Fokus, Norway's fourth biggest bank, has a share exchange offer valuing BNbank at 2.06 billion crowns.
